scores.evidence: Phase 4: Core Features ... Escalation Flow - Route to human agent if uncertain
scores.rationale: Phases run docs→ingestion→pipeline→features→integration, but QA, security, and deployment come last, and escalation/memory are specified after the pipeline with nothing proven first.
The first phase is document prep, not a thin end-to-end production slice; deployment is Phase 7.

scores.evidence: Store in vector database (Pinecone, Weaviate, Chroma, Milvus)
scores.rationale: Options are listed with no defaults, flip conditions, or irreversible-decision gates.
There is no ordering by blast radius within phases; items are flat lists.

scores.evidence: Backend: API endpoints with rate limiting
scores.rationale: Security is barely mentioned (rate limiting only); there is no auth, PII, or injection handling in any phase.
Observability appears only in Phase 7, with analytics in Phase 5, not from day zero.
Doc versioning in Phase 1 and Docker in Phase 7 are minimal, with no threaded reproducibility.

scores.evidence: Fallback Responses - Graceful handling of out-of-scope questions
scores.rationale: Fallback and escalation appear only in a mid-plan feature phase, with no resilience in early phases.
Budgets come last; defenses and human-in-the-loop are not placed before capabilities; memory and feedback are listed after the pipeline, with no ordered layering.
There is no explicit deferred-work list or pull-forward conditions.

note: A generic, feature-ordered RAG outline with no walking skeleton, decision gates, threaded security, or deferred-work list.
